CVE-2024-36971.title: net: fix __dst_negative_advice() race
CVE-2024-36971.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: fix __dst_negative_advice() race

__dst_negative_advice() does not enforce proper RCU rules when
sk->dst_cache must be cleared, leading to possible UAF.

RCU rules are that we must first clear sk->sk_dst_cache,
then call dst_release(old_dst).

Note that sk_dst_reset(sk) is implementing this protocol correctly,
while __dst_negative_advice() uses the wrong order.

Given that ip6_negative_advice() has special logic
against RTF_CACHE, this means each of the three ->negative_advice()
existing methods must perform the sk_dst_reset() themselves.

Note the check against NULL dst is centralized in
__dst_negative_advice(), there is no need to duplicate
it in various callbacks.

Many thanks to Clement Lecigne for tracking this issue.

This old bug became visible after the blamed commit, using UDP sockets.

CVE-2026-104928.title: Kernel object validation bypass in k_thread_stack_space_get syscall verifier with CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS
CVE-2026-104928.description:
The system call verifier z_vrfy_k_thread_stack_space_get() in kernel/thread.c checked the result of K_SYSCALL_OBJ(thread, K_OBJ_THREAD) with the CHECKIF() macro instead of K_OOPS(). CHECKIF() compiles to if (0) when CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS is selected, and becomes an assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT_ON_ERRORS is selected. In both cases, the kernel-object validation result for the user-supplied thread pointer is ignored, or is a no-op when assertions are disabled.

On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE, CONFIG_INIT_STACKS and CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO plus one of those check modes, a user-mode thread can call k_thread_stack_space_get() with an arbitrary pointer. That pointer can be a fake struct k_thread in its own memory, or a thread object it has no permission on. z_impl_k_thread_stack_space_get() then dereferences thread->stack_info in supervisor mode and scans memory starting at the attacker-chosen stack_info.start.

CVE-2026-128979.title: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signatures in libdigidocpp
CVE-2026-128979.description:
Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc4, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on Android, and Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on iOS.

The vulnerability occurs because libdigidocpp does not properly validate
the Extended Key Usage (EKU) extension of certificates used to sign
OCSP responses. Specifically, it fails to verify that the certificate
contains the id-kp-OCSPSigning EKU, which identifies certificates
authorised to sign OCSP responses.

This issue affects libdigidocpp: from 3.10.0 before 4.5.2; DigiDoc4: from 4.0.0 before 4.11.2; DigiDoc: from 3.0.0 before 3.2.0; DigiDoc: from 3.0.1 before 3.2.0.

CVE-2026-99390.title: xfs: fix correction of unwritten extents in quota file data fork
CVE-2026-99390.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix correction of unwritten extents in quota file data fork

LOLLM noticed a couple of problems with the code that fixes unwritten
mappings in the quota file's data fork: first, we should zero the ondisk
contents as part of converting them to "unwritten" just in case we crash
shortly after the conversion. Second, and more importantly, it noticed
that we fail to resynchronize the iext tree cursor after modifying the
iext tree. If the tree shape changes, we could be in a world of hurt.
Third, we should force a quotacheck if we reset an ondisk dquot. Fix
all issues.
